claim: Code tokens split into two categories by loss/perplexity: 'challenging' tokens that are difficult to predict (concentrated at the beginning of a code block) and 'confident' tokens that are easily inferred.
stance_target: token-level uncertainty proxies (loss/perplexity) contain real structural signal about where code generation is risky
scope_conditions: systematic study of code-token loss distributions, AAAI 2024 acceptance
quoted_support: With an analysis of loss distributions of code tokens, we find that code tokens can be divided into two categories: challenging tokens that are difficult to predict and confident tokens that can be easily inferred.

claim: AdapT sampling, which applies a larger temperature to challenging tokens and a smaller temperature to confident tokens, significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art decoding strategy across LLMs of different sizes on two popular code-generation datasets.
stance_target: uncertainty-triggered decoding-time interventions yield measurable code-generation payoffs
scope_conditions: multiple LLM sizes, two benchmark datasets, published AAAI 2024
quoted_support: We apply AdapT sampling to LLMs with different sizes and conduct evaluations on two popular datasets. Results show that AdapT sampling significantly outperforms state-of-the-art decoding strategy.

claim: AdapT establishes an AAAI main-track precedent for papers that convert a token-level uncertainty proxy into a decoding-time control action for code generation, evidencing venue fit for this class of prescriptive method.
stance_target: AAAI venue precedent for the target paper's methodological genre
quoted_support: This paper is accepted by AAAI 2024
